build_cmd: find /build -name '*.o' -size 0 -delete 2>/dev/null; tc-sync-mtimes /build/.tc_md5 src tests && sed 's/passed += run_test(test, test->_name, custom_allocate);/{ bool tc_ok = run_test(test, test->_name, custom_allocate); printf("TCRESULT %s %s\\n", tc_ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", test->_name); fflush(stdout); passed += tc_ok; }/' tests/main.cpp > /build/tc_main.new && (cmp -s /build/tc_main.new /build/tc_main.cpp || mv /build/tc_main.new /build/tc_main.cpp) && rm -f /build/o/test && make -s -j4 -f Makefile BUILD=/build/o CXXFLAGS='-O1 -std=c++11 -Itests' SOURCES="src/pugixml.cpp $(ls tests/*.cpp | grep -v -e tests/fuzz_ -e tests/main.cpp | tr '\n' ' ') /build/tc_main.cpp" /build/o/test 2>&1 | grep -E 'error' | head -40; test -x /build/o/test
notes: pugixml's own test runner (tests/main.cpp) only prints failures, so build_cmd writes a copy to /build/tc_main.cpp (sed) that prints 'TCRESULT PASS|FAIL <test>' per test, and builds the suite with the repo Makefile into /build (volume) at -O1 without -g/-Werror. Tests run from /w so tests/data paths resolve. tc-sync-mtimes touches content-changed sources because the harness restores files with their old mtimes.
